## Data Download

```{python}
dataset = "thedevastator/billboard-hot-100-audio-features"
files = ["Hot Stuff.csv", "Hot 100 Audio Features.csv"]
```

### the genre column has multiple different genres associates with each song. ex ['dance pop', 'pop', 'post-teen pop'], we want to change this just a single string

```{python}
def first_genre(val):
    # if the column is empty/null/none, it returns NaN
    if pd.isna(val):
        return np.nan
    # real list/tuple already
    if isinstance(val, (list, tuple)):
        return val[0] if len(val) else np.nan
    # try to parse string like "['dance pop','pop']" or '["dance pop","pop"]'
    s = str(val).strip()
    try:
        parsed = ast.literal_eval(s)
        if isinstance(parsed, (list, tuple)) and parsed:
            return parsed[0]
    except Exception:
        pass
    # if it's a comma-separated string, take the first part
    if "," in s:
        return s.split(",")[0].strip().strip("'").strip('"')
    # otherwise just return as-is
    return s

# keep original, write cleaned value to a new column
df_final["primary_genre"] = df_final["spotify_genre"].apply(first_genre)

```

## Start of EDA
### Table 1: Summary of audio features by Top 10 status

```{python}
# Table 1: average audio feature values for Top 10 vs. non-Top 10 songs
# (training data only)
table_1 = (
    train_df
    .groupby("top_10")[["danceability", "energy", "valence", "loudness", "tempo"]]
    .mean()
    .round(2)
)

# add number of songs in each group
table_1.insert(0, "Number of songs", train_df["top_10"].value_counts().sort_index())

# readable labels
table_1.index = ["Not Top 10", "Top 10"]
table_1.columns = ["Number of songs", "Danceability", "Energy", "Valence",
                   "Loudness (dB)", "Tempo (BPM)"]
table_1
```

### Figure 1: Class balance of Top 10 vs. non-Top 10 songs

```{python}
# Figure 1: number of songs that did and did not reach the Top 10
# (training data only)
class_counts = (
    train_df["top_10"]
    .map({0: "Not Top 10", 1: "Top 10"})
    .value_counts()
    .reset_index()
)
class_counts.columns = ["Top 10 status", "Number of songs"]

alt.Chart(class_counts).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("Top 10 status", title="Top 10 status", axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0)),
    y=alt.Y("Number of songs", title="Number of songs"),
    color=alt.Color("Top 10 status", legend=None)
).properties(
    width=300,
    height=300,
    title="Number of songs that reached the Top 10 (training data)"
)
```
